title: I2C on the Uno at 400 kHz. You use 100 kΩ pull-ups instead of 4.7 kΩ. What can go wrong?
options: The rising edges are too slow, so bits are read wrong or the LCD is silent
The master can no longer pull SDA low
Nothing, a bigger value is always better
explain: A pull-up and the bus capacitance make an RC circuit. Big R means a slow rise. At 400 kHz the line does not reach HIGH in time. Small R gives fast edges but more current when a device pulls low. 2.2 kΩ to 10 kΩ is normal.

title: Label buffer for the LCD. What does this print?
explain: snprintf writes at most size-1 characters and then a '\0'. So buf holds "123". The return value is the length it WANTED to write: 5. If n >= sizeof buf, the text was cut. Always check it.

title: Simulated PRIMASK. log_event() is called inside your critical section. What does this print?
options: 1, interrupts are ON again too early
explain: unlock() in log_event() turns interrupts on, but the outer code is still in its critical section. Fix: save the old state in lock() and restore THAT state in unlock(), not always 'on'. This is what critical-section crates do.

title: A u8 pulse counter is at 250. What do these three lines print?
explain: wrapping_add wraps around: 260 - 256 = 4. saturating_add stops at 255. checked_add returns None on overflow. A plain + panics in debug and wraps in release. In firmware, choose the behavior on purpose.

title: You replace the 10 kΩ pot on A0 with a 1 MΩ pot. Readings get noisy and lag behind. Why?
options: The ADC sampling capacitor needs a low source impedance (about 10 kΩ or less)
The ADC only accepts 10 kΩ parts
The pot burns out at 5 V
explain: The ADC charges a small capacitor through your source resistance. With 1 MΩ it does not settle in the sample time, so values are wrong and depend on the last channel. Use a lower value pot, or add a buffer or a 100 nF cap at the pin.

title: Uno has 2 KB SRAM. Your sketch has many Serial.println("long text...") lines and acts strange. What helps?
options: Serial.println(F("text")) keeps the text in flash
Make the strings global const char[]
explain: On AVR, string literals are copied into SRAM at start, because flash is a separate address space. Many texts fill the 2 KB and the stack hits the data. F() keeps the text in flash and reads it when printing. A plain const char[] still lives in SRAM.

title: Serial command buffer. Sometimes a nearby variable changes. Tap the bug.
explain: buf has indexes 0 to 7. With idx == 8 the check <= 8 passes and buf[8] is written: one byte past the array. Use idx < sizeof buf.

title: I2C LCD is blank: 5 checks
bullets: Pins: Uno hardware I2C is A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL), not D4/D5.
Address: run a scanner. 0x27 and 0x3F are common. Wrong address = no ACK.
Pull-ups: 2.2 to 10 kΩ on SDA and SCL to VCC. Not 100 kΩ.
Power and GND: shared ground, correct supply (5 V for most LCD backpacks).
Code: Wire.begin() and lcd.begin() called, and the check of endTransmission() is not removed.

pr.title: Remove unused variable
pr.author: copilot
pr.body: The compiler may warn about err. Simplify send_cmd and always return 0.

explain: endTransmission() returns 0 on success and an error code (for example 2 = NACK on address) otherwise. The PR throws it away, so callers can never see a missing LCD. The variable was used. Keep the return value.

title: SPI mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0). When does the slave sample MOSI?
options: On the rising edge of SCK, the clock idles LOW
On the falling edge of SCK, the clock idles HIGH
On the falling edge, the clock idles LOW
explain: Mode 0: the clock idles low and data is sampled on the first (rising) edge. The master changes MOSI on the falling edge. If your sensor expects mode 3 and you use mode 0, bytes come out shifted or wrong. Check the datasheet.

title: UART 115200 baud, 8N1. About how many bytes per second can you send?
explain: 8N1 sends 10 bits for each byte: 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop. 115200 / 10 = 11520 bytes per second. Not 115200 / 8. About 87 µs per byte.
